Article Title: 'First you broke their bones, now filing FIRs': Rahul Gandhi warns PM Modi, Amit Shah to not 'threaten Gen Z into silence'
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi took a jab at PM Modi and Amit Shah, calling them 'India's past'

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the action against student protesters, alleging that the government was trying to "silence Gen Z" through FIRs and social media takedowns after directly attacking them during protests.Making a statement on X, the Congress leader said, "PM Modi and Amit Shah - you cannot threaten Gen Z into silence. First you broke their bones. Now you are filing FIRs and taking down their accounts."Further taking a jab at PM Modi and Shah, he added, "You are India’s past. Be careful about how you treat India’s future."This comes a day after Rahul demanded a Supreme Court-monitored, high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police action against student protesters during the July 20 demonstration at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.In a post on X, the Congress MP had called for an impartial probe into the alleged use of force, saying, "Students deserve justice. An independent SC-monitored high-powered committee must be constituted to probe brutalities against our students."Gandhi also shared a video purportedly showing police action against the protesters. The footage appeared to show police personnel lathi-charging demonstrators, while another clip showed a man in civilian clothes forcefully pushing a student carrying the Indian flag onto the road.His demand came as Opposition MPs from several INDIA bloc parties staged a protest at Makar Dwar in the Parliament complex over the alleged police action against students and the alleged embezzlement of donations meant for the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.The MPs gathered around 10.30 am, carrying placards questioning who ordered the police action at Jantar Mantar and raising slogans demanding accountability from the Centre over the alleged use of force and the alleged financial irregularities in donations to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple.The protest took place hours before the Rajya Sabha was scheduled to consider and pass the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses PM Modi and Amit Shah of trying to "silence Gen Z" through FIRs and social media takedowns after directly attacking them during protests. This comes a day after Rahul demanded a Supreme Court-monitored, high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police action.

Article Title: Parts of Manusmriti now part of 'curriculum', says Mallikarjun Kharge
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge speaks in Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon Session of Parliament, in New Delhi

NEW DELHI: The debate on Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill in RS Thursday turned into a heated argument between treasury benches and opposition when leader of the opposition Mallikarjun Kharge read out what he claimed Hindi translation of a portion from Manusmriti.Kharge alleged portions of Manusmriti have become part of the "curriculum" under BJP govt. He was challenged by leader of the House J P Nadda, who asked the LoP to produce the "original manuscript" for authentication.RS chairperson CP Radhakrishnan asked Kharge what Manusmriti had to do with the bill. Kharge claimed, "Manusmriti teaches that if a 'Shudra' listens to Veda, his ears should be filled with shards; if he reads Ved aloud, his tongue should be cut off; and if he retains its words, his body should be dismembered."BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi slammed Kharge citing B R Ambedkar's writings to argue there was no untouchability in the era of Manu.
Article Summary: Opposition leader of the opposition Mallikarjun Kharge read out what he claimed Hindi translation of a portion from Manusmriti. He was challenged by leader of House J P Nadda, who asked the LoP to produce the "original manuscript" for authentication.

Article Title: NEET leak row: Opposition politicising issue, government has brought in strict law, says BJP
Article Text:
BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi speaks in the Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament, in New Delhi

NEW DELHI: Treasury bench MPs condemned opposition for politicising the NEET-UG paper leak issue and recent protests, as they highlighted how govt has taken steps in the right direction to address concerns by holding dialogue with students to end their agitation and proposing a stronger law against exam paper leaks.Participating in the discussion, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi listed government's efforts to resolve student protest and also highlighted how senior ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh held talks with them and activist Sonam Wangchuk, who was fasting for 26 days.Government agreed to the demands of students, he said, adding Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister, a fast-track court was set up and a task force was set up by PM Narendra Modi under Aadhaar architect Nandan Nilekani.On Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, Trivedi said there are three basic principles - a sensitive approach towards students, a secured process and a stringent law against paper leaks. Trivedi said the bill provides for stringent punishment, time-bound investigation and speedier justice. These will prove key in preventing paper leaks, he said.Targeting opposition MPs, who raised questions on PM Modi's educational qualifications, he said those who have never themselves faced competition in exams, in education, or in their own political parties are now teaching the govt. "In contrast, our politicians and our PM have faced competition and exams and have risen from the ground," Trivedi said.JDU's Sanjay Jha supported the bill, saying this should not be looked at from political prospects.Shiv Sena's Milind Deora suggested students should be involved in the reform process by giving them a formal role in the consultations.
Article Summary: Treasury bench MPs condemned opposition for politicising the NEET-UG paper leak issue and recent protests. They highlighted how govt has taken steps in the right direction to address concerns. BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi listed government's efforts to resolve student protest.

Article Title: BJP submits breach of privilege notice against Rahul Gandhi
Article Text:
File photo: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Accusing leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi of demeaning the Parliament's dignity and making offensive remarks against citizens with his "idiots" and "andhbhakts" jibes in Lok Sabha, BJP on Thursday submitted a notice of "breach of privilege and contempt of the House" against him with Speaker Om Birla and has sought his unconditional apology to the House and Union home minister Amit Shah."No allegation of a defamatory or incriminatory nature shall be made by a member against any person unless the member has given adequate advance notice to the Speaker and also to the minister concerned," BJP MP Anurag Thakur wrote to Birla citing Lok Sabha rules and urging the matter be sent to the privilege committee for inquiry as Rahul violated them.BJP chief whip Sanjay Jaiswal has also submitted a separate complaint to Birla against the LoP, seeking action against him for allegedly violating several rules guiding an MP's conduct in LS.Jaiswal said, "While strong criticism of the govt policy is a legitimate and essential feature of parliamentary democracy, personal attacks and the use of language that is insulting, defamatory or otherwise unparliamentary cannot be permitted within the proceedings of this august House."Rahul in his address Wednesday, during discussion on a bill that proposes more stringent punishment against the guilty in exam paper leaks, had held Shah responsible for the alleged police's excesses against protesters on July 20, drawing vehement protest from the treasury members and his speech was cut short as he stuck to the charge.Some of his remarks were deemed unparliamentary and expunged from the records.Thakur noted that Speaker Om Birla repeatedly "warned" Rahul but he repeated the unparliamentary words.
Article Summary: BJP MP Anurag Thakur wrote to Speaker Om Birla citing Lok Sabha rules. He urged the matter be sent to the privilege committee for inquiry as Rahul violated them. Rahul had held Shah responsible for the alleged police's excesses against protesters.

Article Title: Despite unrest, PM Modi, Amit Shah haven't spoken on NEET protests: Opposition
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A political storm erupted in Rajya Sabha on Thursday after Congress chief and LoP Mallikarjun Kharge raised questions over home minister Amit Shah 's absence and his silence on the police brutality on protesting students, saying "ek din bahar kheench ke layenge... janata ke beech (one day we will drag you out before people)".This drew strong objections from leader of the House JP Nadda and treasury members who accused Kharge of using unparliamentary language. Later, BJP slammed the RS LoP for "threatening" to incite violence against Shah.Kharge picked up from where Rahul Gandhi had left off in LS Wednesday, in what is being seen in certain BJP quarters as a confirmation of a plan by Congress to target Shah.Faced with angry protests, Kharge in RS clarified that he meant "Jan shakti (people's power) will drag him out to make him accountable. I never meant physically dragging him out."Speaking on Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, Kharge slammed absence of PM Narendra Modi and Shah from RS, saying they hadn't spoken anything despite so much unrest. "Despite so much unrest, you are not opening your mouth.Has someone stitched it?" he asked.Though opposition MPs did not oppose the bill, members questioned if the increased penalty and jail terms will stop paper leak. CPM's John Brittas flagged when the anti-paper leak bill was first introduced in 2024, govt claimed it would put an end to menace, but there have been more cases of paper leaks.RJD's Manoj Jha said that lawmakers merely using Gen Z words in their speeches in the House and making cosmetic changes won't help.MPs from DMK, AIADMK and Samajwadi Party demanded govt scrap NEET as "one size suits all" formula won't work for entire country.
Article Summary: Congress chief and LoP Mallikarjun Kharge raised questions over home minister Amit Shah's absence and his silence on the police brutality on protesting students. He said "ek din bahar kheench ke layenge... janata ke beech (one day we will drag you out before people)". This drew strong objections from leader of the House JP Nadda and treasury members.

Article Title: Delhi high court seeks police reply on Umar Khalid's 3rd bail appeal in 2020 riots conspiracy case
Article Text:
The Delhi high court has sought responses from the Delhi Police regarding Umar Khalid's bail appeal.





NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Friday sought responses from the Delhi Police on activist and former JNU scholar Umar Khalid's appeal.The appeal challenges the trial court's July 4 order rejecting his third regular bail plea in the alleged larger conspiracy case linked to the 2020 North-East Delhi riots.A Division Bench of Justice Prathiba M Singh and Justice Vikas Mahajan also issued notice on Khalid's application seeking interim bail and fixed August 27 for hearing both the appeal and the interim bail plea.Senior advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Khalid, told the court that the appeal challenges the trial court's order dismissing his third regular bail application.Additional solicitor general SV Raju represented the Delhi Police.Khalid has sought interim bail pending the Supreme Court's decision on the legal question of whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override the restrictions on grant of bail under Section 43D(5) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).In his appeal, Khalid argued that despite more than six months having passed since the Supreme Court rejected his earlier bail plea on January 5, 2026, there has been no meaningful progress in the trial, news agency ANI reported.He submitted that arguments on framing of charges are still underway and that he has remained in custody since September 2020.On July 4, additional sessions Judge Sameer Bajpai of the Karkardooma Court dismissed the regular bail pleas of Umar Khalid and co-accused Sharjeel Imam.The trial court held that the fresh bail applications were not maintainable in view of the Supreme Court's earlier order, which had allowed them to renew their bail pleas only after the examination of the protected witnesses relied upon by the prosecution or after one year, whichever occurred earlier.The prosecution opposed the bail pleas, contending that there had been no substantial change in circumstances since the Supreme Court's previous order, ANI reported.The case stems from FIR 59/2020 registered by the Delhi Police Special Cell over the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 North-East Delhi riots. The trial remains at the stage of arguments on framing of charges, with charges yet to be framed.The Delhi high court has also listed co-accused Sharjeel Imam's appeal against the rejection of his bail plea for hearing on August 27.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: The Delhi high court has sought responses from the Delhi Police regarding Umar Khalid's bail appeal. The appeal challenges the trial court's July 4 order rejecting his third regular bail plea in the alleged larger conspiracy case linked to the 2020 North-East Delhi riots. The trial remains at the stage of arguments on framing of charges, with charges yet to be framed.

Article Title: 'No reason to invoke criminal justice machinery': CJP's Saurav Das on use of derogatory language by protesters
Article Text:
CJP spokesperson Saurav Das and Ruchika Singh (R)

Zero FIR

against Noida woman





NEW DELHI: Reacting to the alleged use of derogatory remarks by CJP protesters during the Jantar Mantar agitation, party spokesperson Saurav Das said those offended by such language were free to pursue legal remedies for defamation but argued that criminal proceedings against protesters over objectionable speech were not appropriate."If any language used was derogatory in nature, then the person concerned is free to pursue civil and criminal defamation proceedings against the individual concerned. However, the use of the criminal justice machinery against protesters is highly condemnable, and no one should be punished merely for using objectionable language."Also read: 'Raised with core values': Lawyer who filed complaint against Noida woman over 'abusive' remarks against PM "The language may be wrong, and it may be objectionable to someone, but that is no reason to invoke the criminal justice machinery against such people. It creates a chilling effect. I don't think this is acceptable to anybody, especially the younger generation."Adding further, he said, "I would request the younger generation to be very careful about the words they use and the kind of insults or remarks they make against people in general.""That said, the use of the criminal justice machinery is a big no-no. It is completely unacceptable and should not happen. We would also like to tell the police to remain calm and not misuse their powers for any political ends."His remarks came after Noida Police registered a Zero FIR against a woman accused of using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.According to police, the FIR was lodged at the Expressway police station on the complaint of Smriti Singh, a resident of Ghaziabad, against Ruchika Singh, a resident of Sector 168 in Noida.The complainant alleged that on July 23, the accused used "abusive and objectionable" language against the prime minister at Jantar Mantar, hurting the dignity of the constitutional office and intending to spread hatred and disturb public peace.Police registered the case under Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Additional deputy commissioner of Police (Noida) Manisha Singh said the complaint had been registered as a Zero FIR and would be transferred to Delhi Police for further investigation.A Zero FIR allows a complaint to be registered at any police station regardless of where the alleged offence took place. It is subsequently transferred to the police station with jurisdiction over the case.
Article Summary: CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said those offended by such language were free to pursue legal remedies for defamation. He argued that criminal proceedings against protesters over objectionable speech were not appropriate. His remarks came after Noida Police registered a Zero FIR against a woman accused of using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Article Title: Eight of family injured after Tempo Traveller rams into parked truck on Mumbai-Nashik Highway in Bhiwandi
Article Text:
Four passengers who sustained minor injuries were treated and discharged, while the four seriously injured were given primary treatment before being taken by their relatives to Jalgaon for further medical care

TOI





Bhiwandi: Eight members of a family from Chalisgaon in Jalgaon district were injured, four of them seriously, after the Tempo Traveller they were travelling in rammed into a parked truck on Mumbai-Nashik Highway near Sonale village in Bhiwandi taluka on Thursday early morning.According to Bhiwandi Taluka police, the Sheikh family had travelled to Mumbai airport to drop two relatives, who were leaving for Umrah pilgrimage. The accident occurred while they were returning to Chalisgaon.Tausif, the driver of the Tempo Traveller, toldthat heavy rainfall had drastically reduced visibility on the highway. He said two vehicles were moving ahead of him, and while attempting to overtake them from the left, he mistook a truck parked on the roadside for a moving vehicle. Before he could react, the Tempo Traveller crashed into the rear of the truck.Following the accident, local residents rushed to the spot and shifted all the injured to Indira Gandhi Memorial Hospital in Bhiwandi. Four passengers who sustained minor injuries were treated and discharged, while the four seriously injured were given primary treatment before being taken by their relatives to Jalgaon for further medical care.The injured alleged that the truck driver had parked the vehicle on the roadside without switching on the hazard indicators, and claimed that the absence of warning lights, coupled with poor visibility due to heavy rain, led to the accident.Senior police inspector Harshvardhan Barve of Bhiwandi Taluka police station said the injured had left for their native place with relatives before their statements could be recorded. “An FIR will be registered after recording the statements of the injured, and appropriate action will be taken against the person found responsible,” he said.
Article Summary: Eight members of a family from Chalisgaon in Jalgaon district were injured, four of them seriously. The Tempo Traveller they were travelling in rammed into a parked truck on Mumbai-Nashik Highway near Sonale village in Bhiwandi taluka on Thursday early morning.

Article Title: Re-NEET row: Bombay high court finds no discrepancy in answer sheets, dismisses 2 petitions; imposes Rs 5,000 fine
Article Text:
The Bombay High Court dismissed four petitions challenging the re-NEET examination results

(With ANI inputs)





Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar bench of the Bombay high court has dismissed two petitions challenging the re-NEET examination results after examining the original answer sheets and finding no discrepancies in the evaluation.The court also imposed a fine of Rs 5,000 on each petitioner for approaching it with what it termed incorrect and unverified claims.The petitions had alleged that the National Testing Agency NTA ) declared incorrect results and made errors while evaluating the answer sheets.The matter was heard by a division bench of Justice N. B. Suryawanshi and Justice A. D. Shinde.Taking note of the seriousness of the allegations, the bench directed that the original answer sheets of the concerned students be brought from Delhi in sealed envelopes.The court examined the answer sheets and also allowed the students, their parents and their lawyers to inspect the original records.After scrutinising the material, the court found that the marks awarded by the NTA and the declared results matched the original answer sheets, with no errors or discrepancies in the evaluation.Senior panel advocate Rohit Sarvagya, appearing for the Centre and the NTA, produced all the original documents before the court during the hearing.After considering the submissions and examining the original records, the bench dismissed two petitions and imposed a cost of Rs 5,000 on each petitioner for filing the pleas based on incorrect and unverified information.With the high court's ruling, the re-NEET examination results declared by the NTA have received judicial confirmation.
Article Summary: The Bombay High Court dismissed four petitions challenging the re-NEET examination results. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 5,000 on each petitioner for approaching it with what it termed incorrect and unverified claims. The petitions had alleged that the National Testing Agency NTA ) declared incorrect results and made errors while evaluating the answer sheets.

Article Title: Congress stages rasta roko in Kalyan over police action on Jantar Mantar protesters
Article Text:
Congress workers staged a protest in Kalyan West against alleged police action.





KALYAN: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West to protest against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi over the alleged paper leak issue.Led by Navin Singh, Kalyan District President, the protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators by the Delhi Police.Traffic was briefly affected in the area before police intervened.The party also submitted a memorandum to the Kalyan tehsildar, addressed to the President of India, seeking an inquiry into the alleged police action against students and Congress leaders, including Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other party leaders, during the protest at Delhi.In the memorandum, the Congress demanded the immediate resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, holding him morally responsible for the alleged irregularities in the paper leak. The party also sought an urgent discussion in Parliament on alleged examination irregularities and issues affecting students' future.The memorandum further demanded that all FIRs and criminal cases registered against students and peaceful protesters be withdrawn immediately.Among those present at the protest were corporator Samina Sheikh, former corporator Iftekar Khan and other Congress office-bearers and workers. Police maintained security at the protest site and ensured traffic movement was restored after the demonstration concluded.
Article Summary: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West. They were protesting against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators.

Article Title: Bank manager among 2 more held in 23cr gold loan scam
Article Text: Nagpur: The Economic Offences Branch of Nagpur police has apprehended two more persons in the 23 crore gold loan scam at a bank, taking the number of arrests in the case to seven.The arrested individuals are Ashish Wanjari (43), a resident of Aradhana Nagar, who worked as a manager at the bank's Narsala branch, and the then sub-branch manager Prakash Awasthi (34), a resident of Prashant Nagar. Investigating officer Santosh Tokalwad will produce the duo in court on Friday and seek their police custody. Those arrested earlier included Dinesh Nagpure of Shesh Nagar, Pramod Tete, Rajendra Shilanakar, Pankaj Kekatpure and Nandu Kharavde.The probe is being conducted under deputy commissioner of police (DCP) Deepak Aggrawal. Investigations are underway to uncover the full extent of the conspiracy and identify any other accused involved.
Article Summary: The Economic Offences Branch of Nagpur police has apprehended two more persons in the 23 crore gold loan scam at a bank. The arrested individuals are Ashish Wanjari (43), a resident of Aradhana Nagar, and Prakash Awasthi (34) The duo will produce the duo in court on Friday and seek their police custody.

Article Title: Educationist and BJP functionary arrested in fake Shalarth ID case
Article Text:
A team of Nashik police tak educationist Sanjay Garud into custody from a farmhouse in a village in Solapur district on Monday.

Nashik:





The city police on Monday arrested a well-known educationist from Jalgaon in the fake Shalarth ID case on Monday.The accused has been identified as Sanjay Garud, who is a also a BJP functionary and resident of Shendurni in Jamner taluka of Jalgaon district. This marks the sixth arrest in the case registered with the Nashik Road police station in March this year.An officer from the Nashik city police said 67-year-old Garud was evading arrest. “On Monday, he was arrested from a farmhouse in Natepute in Solapur district in connection with the case registered on March 12, 2026, for offences punishable under Sections 318(4) (Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property), 316(2) (criminal breach of trust), 316(5) (covering specific breach of trust), 336(2)(3) (forgery of documents or electronic record) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy to commit serious offence) among other sections of the BNS and the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000. ”ACP (crime) Sandeep Mitke said the scam involves systematic embezzlement of govt funds amounting to Rs160 crore under the jurisdiction of deputy director of education (Nashik division), covering Nashik, Jalgaon, Dhule and Nandurbar districts.He said a total of 841 teaching and non-teaching staff members were illegally included into the official ‘Shalarth’ salary system. Without submitting the mandatory individual approval proposals to the education department, the accused forged backdated appointment orders and drafted fraudulent entries into the payroll software to siphon off monthly salaries and arrear payments.So far, around 1,200 individuals, including school principals, trust operators, former deputy directors of education, education officers and pay superintendents, have been identified as suspects.Sanjay Garud operates 15 school institutions. The investigation by the Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by Mitke has found that fake individual approvals were issued for 177 staff members across his schools, even though no valid approval proposals were ever received or processed by the education officer’s department.Following confidential intelligence and precise technical tracking, the Nashik crime branch discovered that Garud was taking refuge at a farmhouse in Solapur. Under the guidance of Mitke, a specialised team comprising sub-inspector Chetan Shrivant and officers Pravin Waghmare, Mahesh Salunkhe, Uttam Pawar, Milindsingh Pardeshi and Nazim Khan Pathan raided the location.On being asked about the arrest, water resources minister Girish Mahajan said he was taking information about the same.
Article Summary: The accused has been identified as Sanjay Garud, a also a BJP functionary and resident of Shendurni in Jamner taluka of Jalgaon district. This marks the sixth arrest in the case registered with the Nashik Road police station in March this year.

Article Title: War of words between Anbumani and Manickam Tagore over Mekedatu issue
Article Text:
War of Words

Chennai:





A war of words has broke out between PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss and TNCC president Manickam Tagore over the Mekedatu issue after the former equated Congress with BJP alleging that both parties were `trying to betray TN in the Mekedatu issue.’Anbumani dared leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi to speak in favour of Tamil Nadu in the Mekedatu issue. “Can Rahul support Tamil Nadu in the Mekedatu issue and can he say that Karnataka shouldn’t construct Mekedatu dam during his visit to Chennai on Aug 1?” Anbumani asked. “If Rahul speaks for TN, I will quit NDA .”He was responding to Manickam Tagore who demanded that Anbumani speak against BJP in the parliament since he was alleging that BJP had also betrayed TN. The two leaders also traded charges that their parties had won seats in the assembly election due to support from their allies. While Anbumani said Congress would not even win a councillor’s post on its own strength, Tagore retorted saying PMK won four assembly seats because of its allies AIADMK and BJP.The two leaders also had differences over chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s proposed visit to Karnataka.
Article Summary: Anbumani Ramadoss dared leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi to speak in favour of Tamil Nadu in the Mekedatu issue. The two leaders also traded charges that their parties had won seats in the assembly election due to support from their allies.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Financial irregularities stalled Wadakkanchery LIFE Mission project: CBI
Article Text:
The chargesheet, filed before Ernakulam CJM court, has named six persons as accused

Kochi:





CBI has filed a preliminary chargesheet in the Wadakkanchery LIFE Mission case.The chargesheet, filed before the Ernakulam CJM court, alleges that financial irregularities in the execution of the housing project ultimately stalled it.The chargesheet also names six persons as accused. Among the accused are Sandeep Nair, Swapna Suresh and UAE Consulate PRO P S Sarith — all named as accused in the 2020 gold smuggling case as well — apart from Santhosh Eappen of UNITAC Builders.Though M Sivasankar, former principal secretary to the then chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, was on the accused list in the FIR, he has not been named in the preliminary chargesheet. Investigation into the role of govt officials including Sivasankar was ongoing, sources said.The case pertains to the LIFE Mission housing project in Wadakkanchery, Thrissur. The project was funded through a Rs 21-crore contribution from UAE Red Crescent with an aim to rehabilitate families affected by the 2018 Kerala floods.In the chargesheet, CBI has alleged that financial diversion prevented beneficiaries from availing the promised housing.Former Wadakkanchery MLA Anil Akkara was the complainant in the case. He had alleged violations under Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) apart from corruption in connection with the handling of foreign funds received for the project.Vigilance and anti-corruption bureau (VACB) is also investigating the case.
Article Summary: The case pertains to the LIFE Mission housing project in Wadakkanchery, Thrissur. The project was funded through a Rs 21-crore contribution from UAE Red Crescent with an aim to rehabilitate families affected by the 2018 Kerala floods.

Article Title: Case against teacher after caning video goes viral
Article Text:
pic for representational purpose only

Thrissur





: Police have registered a case against a social science teacher at Govt Higher Secondary School, Varavoor, near Cheruthuruthy, after allegations that he brutally caned a Class IX student. Women and child welfare minister Bindu Krishna has also ordered an inquiry after a video of the alleged assault surfaced on social media.According to school headmistress K Sethukutty, the incident occurred about two weeks ago, but came to the school’s notice only on Thursday when a video, allegedly recorded by students inside the classroom, went viral.The teacher, Manikandan , a resident of Kanjarassery in Mullurkara, has been serving at the school for the past 18 years. He is visually challenged.The student’s parents, who live at Chembikunnu Unnathi in Varavoor panchayat, said they realised the seriousness of the assault only after watching the video. They subsequently lodged complaints with the school authorities, the police and the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights.Sethukutty said the teacher had been asked to submit an explanation. “We have forwarded the parents’ complaint and the teacher’s explanation to higher authorities in the general education department,” she said.“The department will decide on further action.”A PTA meeting convened on Thursday discussed the incident and recommended action against the teacher. “We will examine the reports and initiate appropriate action on Friday,” said deputy director of education, T Shyla.Officials at the Cheruthuruthy Police Station said a case had been registered based on the parents’ complaint. Police have visited the school and conducted preliminary inquiries.Minister Bindu Krishna has directed the district child protection officer to conduct an urgent inquiry and submit a report. She has also sought a report from the secretary of the general education department.
Article Summary: Police have registered a case against a social science teacher at Govt Higher Secondary School, Varavoor, near Cheruthuruthy, after allegations that he brutally caned a Class IX student. Women and child welfare minister Bindu Krishna has also ordered an inquiry after a video of the alleged assault surfaced on social media.

Article Title: HC sets aside VACB order in favour of ADGP Sreejith
Article Text:
S Sreejith

Kochi

:





The high court has set aside the vigilance report, filed in compliance with its earlier directive to consider the complaint alleging that ADGP S Sreejith had attended the inauguration of a private enterprise abroad in police uniform, holding that the complainant was denied a fair opportunity of hearing.Justice A Badharudeen directed the additional chief secretary (vigilance department) to reconsider the complaint after granting the complainant a personal hearing in the absence of Sreejith and to pass fresh orders within three weeks. The court was considering a petition filed by the complainant, Dipin Edavana of Kannur, an assistant motor vehicle inspector, seeking to quash the vigilance report.Earlier, HC had directed the department to consider Edavana’s complaint and take an appropriate decision within three months. Then, the additional chief secretary had issued a notice asking him to appear for a hearing on April 20. However, he did not attend the hearing, saying that it was proposed as a joint hearing in Sreejith’s presence.Instead, he submitted a representation saying that it was unfair to participate in a joint hearing with the officer against whom he had levelled allegations. Later, the additional chief secretary submitted a report stating that the complainant had failed to cooperate with the enquiry and raised baseless allegations.The court observed that where grave allegations are raised against a person, conducting a joint hearing of the complainant and the person against whom the allegations are made cannot be regarded as a fair procedure. It observed that the complainant may have matters to place before the authority that could implicate the other person and the other person’s presence could inhibit the complainant from presenting his case freely. The court held that the joint hearing had denied the complainant a fair opportunity of being heard and directed the authority to reconsider the complaint afresh.
Article Summary: The high court has set aside the vigilance report, filed in compliance with its earlier directive to consider the complaint alleging that ADGP S Sreejith had attended the inauguration of a private enterprise abroad in police uniform. The court held that the joint hearing had denied the complainant a fair opportunity of being heard and directed the authority to reconsider the complaint afresh.
